summary: Joanny Grosset was an Indologist who earned his Licencié-ès-lettres at the University of Lyon, where he studied under Paul Regnaud.

Joaquim Heliodoro da Cunha Rivara was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied mathematics, philosophy, and medicine at the University of Coimbra (1824–1836) and served as a teacher and librarian at Liceu de Évora (~1838–1855).

Jochem Schindler was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Vienna under Heinz Kronasser (~1962–1967) and earned his Ph.D. at Würzburg (~1967–1972). He taught at Vienna (1972–1974, 1987) and Harvard University (1974–1976, 1978–1987).

Joe Bransford Wilson worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 1984. He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and became Associate Professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb is an archaeologist, Indologist, and Central Asian specialist who studied at Queen Mary and the University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and President of the Royal Numismatic Society (2005–2009).
Joe Currie is an Indology and religious studies scholar affiliated with Harvard University, where he held a post and was a Ph.D. candidate attested in 2026.

Joel Bordeaux is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his BA at Georgia State and his MA, MPhil, and PhD (2015) at Columbia. He held posts at Colgate, Stony Brook, Leiden, Utrecht, and Erasmus University Rotterdam (2025).

Joel Peter Brereton is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held academic posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 2004, and ~2001 professor emeritus).
Joel Tatelman is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford in 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.
Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2010 and 2026.
Joerg Tuske works in philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung is a scholar in computational and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and served as Professor and Dean at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Jogendra Singh was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a historian and Indologist educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (from 1912), and served as University Reader at Patna University (1923).
Johan Andreas dèr Mouw was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern in 1883 and completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1883–1887).

Johan Elverskog is a scholar of Central Asian, Buddhist, and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (BA) and Indiana University Bloomington (MA). He held research posts and became Dedman Family Distinguished Professor at Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist scholar who studied under Antonie Rutgers and Albrecht Weber. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865) and served as Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

Johan Hendrik Gallée was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1866–1873), later teaching at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and Utrecht University.

Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguist who studied at Leiden (Ph.D. 1891), Tübingen, and Leipzig, under Eduard Sievers and August Leskien. He served as professor at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga was a historian, linguist, and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Groningen (1897) and studied at Leipzig and Leiden. He taught at Amsterdam, served as Professor of History at Groningen (1905–1915), and at Leiden (1915–1941).
